chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibrahim ibn Shayba, who said:

I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asking him about completing the prayer in the two Sanctuaries. So he wrote to me: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to love increasing prayer in the two Sanctuaries, so increase in them and complete (do not shorten).'.

key_terms.إِتْمَامِ الصَّلَاةِ: Completing the prayer (performing four rak'ahs instead of two)
key_terms.إِكْثَارَ: Increasing (in frequency or volume of prayer)
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Sanctuaries (Al-Masjid al-Haram and Al-Masjid al-Nabawi)

ai.seo_question: Should I shorten my prayer when visiting Mecca or Medina?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the specific juristic preference (istihbab) for performing full four-rak'ah prayers in the two major Sanctuaries, distinguishing it from the general rule of shortening prayers during travel. It underscores the spiritual merit of these locations by linking the practice directly to the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) personal preference, thereby encouraging believers to maximize their devotional acts in Mecca and Medina.
